bug_description.original: Crash Type: UNKNOWN READ; Crash State: jsoncharutils.h; Sanitizer: undefined (UBSAN).
bug_description.normalized: In simdjson's ondemand floating-point parser, a decimal-only literal can derive an implicit exponent below `smallest_power` without setting `overflow`. The vulnerable `parse_double()` updates `overflow` with the exponent-range check only inside the explicit `e`/`E` branch. For the staged witness, the number starts with `0.`, has 343 fractional digits and no explicit exponent, the 344 digit updates wrap the `uint64_t` accumulator to nonzero `i == 0xca982637f74898bd`, and the leading-zero decimal heuristic clears `overflow` back to false. `parse_double()` then calls `compute_float_64()` with `power == -343`, one below `smallest_power == -342`; `compute_float_64()` cannot take its fast path because `power` is outside `[-22, 22]` and `i` already exceeds `9007199254740991`, the later `i == 0` slow-path return is also skipped because `i` is nonzero, the table index wraps, and the read of `power_of_five_128[index]` causes the saved UBSan SEGV READ.

source.description: First project-code materialization on the vulnerable path reads the first digit of the array element and records that the integer part is zero, enabling the later leading-zero overflow heuristic.
source.value_from: In the staged PoC, the first byte `0xc7` makes `fd.getInt<0, 12>()` yield `action == 4`, and the remaining 347 bytes form one split string whose first array element begins with the decimal token `0.00000000006666...`. This step reads the initial `'0'` of that token, leaving `i == 0` and `leading_zero == true`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-driving value is the implicit decimal exponent computed from the count of fractional digits. For the staged witness, 343 digits after the decimal point make `exponent == -343`.

sink.description: Source-level OOB read sink. The wrapped table index is used to fetch a power-of-five entry far past the precomputed array bounds before the inlined multiply runs.
sink.note: The saved UBSan trace reports the crash at `include/simdjson/generic/jsoncharutils.h:106` inside `full_multiplication()`, which is the inlined multiplication body reached after this caller-side table lookup.

root_cause.code: overflow = overflow || exponent < simdjson::internal::smallest_power || exponent > simdjson::internal::largest_power;
root_cause.description: The exponent-range guard is nested only inside the explicit `e`/`E` branch, so decimal-only numbers skip it even when their implicit exponent is already outside the table's supported range.
root_cause.note: For the witness, `*p` is trailing whitespace rather than `e` or `E`, so this assignment is never executed and `overflow` remains false after the leading-zero heuristic. The fix moves the same range check below the branch so decimal-only numbers also reach it, and adds assertions in `compute_float_64()`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged PoC's first byte is `0xc7`, so `fd.getInt<0, 12>()` yields `action == 4`. The remaining bytes contain no `\n~~\n` separator, so `strings[0]` is the whole JSON fragment beginning with `[0.000...`. The saved crash stack reaches line 40, proving `doc.error()` was false and the first iterated item entered `item.get_double()`.

fine_trace.note: The first character of the numeric array element is `'0'`. Parsing it leaves `i == 0`, and `leading_zero` becomes true, which later enables the decimal-specific overflow correction path.

fine_trace.code: const uint8_t *start_decimal_digits = p; if (!parse_digit(*p, i)) { return NUMBER_ERROR; } p++; while (parse_digit(*p, i)) { p++; } exponent = -(p - start_decimal_digits);
fine_trace.note: The witness has a decimal point followed by 343 fractional digits and no explicit exponent suffix. Together with step 1's initial integer digit, that produces 344 `parse_digit()` updates, wrapping the `uint64_t` accumulator to `i == 0xca982637f74898bd`; after the fractional digits are consumed, `p` points at the trailing space and `exponent` becomes `-343`, one below `simdjson::internal::smallest_power`.

fine_trace.code: overflow = p-src-1 > 19; if (simdjson_unlikely(overflow && leading_zero)) { const uint8_t *start_digits = src + 2; while (*start_digits == '0') { start_digits++; } overflow = start_digits-src > 19; }
fine_trace.note: The raw digit-count heuristic first sets `overflow` because `p - src - 1 == 344 > 19`. The leading-zero correction then skips the 10 zeros after `0.` and resets `overflow` to false because the first non-zero fractional digit is only 12 bytes from `src`.

fine_trace.code: if (*p == 'e' || *p == 'E') { ... overflow = overflow || exponent < simdjson::internal::smallest_power || exponent > simdjson::internal::largest_power; }
fine_trace.note: The token ends at whitespace, so `*p` is neither `e` nor `E` and the explicit-exponent block is skipped. In the vulnerable version, that block contains the only range check that would have noticed `exponent == -343`, so after step 3 `overflow` is still false even though the implicit power is out of range.

fine_trace.code: if (simdjson_likely(!overflow)) { if (compute_float_64(exponent, i, negative, d)) { return d; } }
fine_trace.note: Because `overflow` stayed false, `parse_double()` calls `compute_float_64(exponent, i, negative, d)` with `exponent == -343` and the wrapped accumulator `i == 0xca982637f74898bd` instead of falling back to `parse_float_fallback()`.

The initial exact-conversion fast path does not apply to the witness call. `power == -343` is outside the allowed `[-22, 22]` range, and the wrapped accumulator `i == 0xca982637f74898bd` also exceeds `9007199254740991`, so `compute_float_64()` falls through into its slow-path setup instead of returning from the fast path.

After the fast path fails, the slow-path zero special case is checked. The witness-derived accumulator is `0xca982637f74898bd`, so `i == 0` is false and the function continues toward the table-based slow path instead of returning `0.0`.

With the fast path already rejected and `i != 0`, `compute_float_64()` proceeds to the table index computation. The function assumes the caller already enforced `smallest_power <= power <= largest_power`; here `power == -343`, so `power - smallest_power == -1`, the `uint32_t` cast wraps, and `index` becomes `4294967294`.

The wrapped `index` is used immediately to read `power_of_five_128[index]`, far past the precomputed table. The saved UBSan trace reports the resulting SEGV READ at `jsoncharutils.h:106:41` because the load is inlined into `full_multiplication()`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved UBSan frame points at `jsoncharutils.h:106` because `full_multiplication()` is inlined, but the source-level unsafe read is the caller-side `power_of_five_128[index]` argument evaluation at `numberparsing.h:159`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix moves `overflow = overflow || exponent < smallest_power || exponent > largest_power;` below the optional `e`/`E` block so decimal-only numbers also get the range check before `compute_float_64()` is called, and it adds assertions to `compute_float_64()`.

poc.trigger: The staged witness drives `fuzz_ondemand` down `action == 4`, so the first iterated array item is parsed as a double. That item is a decimal-only token with integer part `0`, 10 leading zero fractional digits, 343 total fractional digits, no explicit exponent, and trailing whitespace; `parse_double()` derives `exponent == -343`, its 344 digit updates wrap the accumulator to nonzero `i == 0xca982637f74898bd`, skips the misplaced exponent-range guard, and crashes when `compute_float_64()` first misses its fast path because `power == -343` is outside `[-22, 22]` and `i` exceeds the exact-mantissa bound, then bypasses the later `i == 0` early return and uses the wrapped table index to read `power_of_five_128`.

format.name: fuzz_ondemand split-input buffer
format.contract: This contract is limited to the saved witness semantics. Byte 0 must remain `0xc7` so `fd.getInt<0, 12>()` yields `action == 4`. The remaining bytes must stay a single split chunk with no `\n~~\n` separator, and its first array element must remain the witnessed decimal-only token that starts with `0.`, contains 343 fractional digits with exactly 10 leading zero fractional digits, has no `e` or `E` suffix, and is followed by whitespace. Those exact properties make `leading_zero` true, clear `overflow` in the decimal-only heuristic, leave `exponent == -343`, and make the wrapped 64-bit accumulator nonzero (`0xca982637f74898bd`), which keeps `compute_float_64()` off its fast path, then bypasses the `i == 0` slow-path exit and reaches the out-of-range `power_of_five_128[index]` lookup before any later structural validation matters.
